name: trans-Pinene hydrate
evidence: Measured in 6 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.17–1.31% of total volatiles (0.034–0.26mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: trans-Pinene hydrate is a botanical molecule, specifically a monoterpene alcohol, that is structurally related to the familiar pine-scented compound pinene. Molecules in this family typically contribute to the complex, woody, or herbal aromas of the aromatic plants that produce them.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in Pimenta racemosa, a member of the myrtle family better known as the West Indian bay tree, which is traditionally used to make bay rum.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Currently, trans-pinene hydrate is a natural compound waiting for its moment in the scientific spotlight. Because it is often just one of many trace molecules in complex plant extracts, researchers have not yet isolated it for dedicated study, meaning there is currently no evidence (Oxford level 5, no evidence) regarding its biological potential.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: There is currently no research literature or evidence available for this specific molecule.
